name: rsa_common_modulus
note: Synthetic textbook RSA common-modulus fixture, not a published historical ciphertext. The same message integer was encrypted with public exponents 17 and 65537 under one modulus. Literal ciphertexts were constructed with Python built-in pow before the attacker was added. Recovery uses only these public integers, extended Euclid, and signed modular powers. The result must reencrypt to both ciphertexts. The original 16-byte encoding includes two leading zero bytes; byte_length records that external encoding information, which RSA integer ciphertexts cannot recover. plaintext_sha256 hashes all 16 recovered raw bytes. No private key is supplied. This certificate does not claim an attack on a configured service, randomized RSA padding, modern cryptography in general, an unknown script, or an unsolved historical challenge.
